title: Microsoft Teams: Facilitator detects open questions and answers them with web search
summary: The briefing accurately reports the planned rollout, licensing prerequisites and meeting opt-in requirement, and distinguishes the notice from existing documentation. The controls are supported; three navigation paths should be extended to show the final configuration choices.

claims.claim: The roadmap feature concerns Microsoft Teams Facilitator detecting and answering questions.
claims.quote: Microsoft Teams: Facilitator detects and answers questions

claims.claim: The record lists Microsoft Teams and Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365).
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Teams", "Microsoft Copilot (Microsoft 365)"]

claims.claim: The roadmap describes automatically detecting unanswered meeting questions and offering web-search help.
claims.quote: Facilitator now automatically detects open questions raised during a Teams meeting and offers to help answer them using web search.

claims.claim: The roadmap example is an unanswered question such as 'What is an LLM?' followed by an offer to find an answer.
claims.quote: When a participant asks a question (e.g., “What is an LLM?”) and no one answers, Facilitator posts a prompt offering to find an answer.

claims.claim: Participants can select 'Yes' to have Facilitator retrieve and share information.
claims.quote: Participants can select “Yes” to have the agent retrieve and share the information.

claims.claim: Learn lists an eligible Microsoft 365 base licence as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: An eligible Microsoft 365 base license.

claims.claim: Learn lists an eligible Microsoft Teams licence as a prerequisite.
claims.quote: Have an eligible Microsoft Teams license.

claims.claim: Learn lists AI-powered Q&A from meeting and web content as generally available.
claims.quote: The following Facilitator capabilities are currently generally available: ... AI-powered Q&A from meeting and web content

claims.claim: The cited Facilitator Learn page does not describe this proactive question-detection behaviour.
claims.quote: Searched: Facilitator proactive question detection knowledge gaps separate admin setting Teams PowerShell policy web search; "Facilitator" "proactive" "web" "policy". Opened microsoftteams/facilitator-teams; it describes prompted Q&A, not unanswered-question detection.

claims.claim: Learn says Facilitator is not supported in external chats and meetings, and the briefing explicitly reports the disagreement with the notice.
claims.quote: Currently, Facilitator isn't supported in 1:1 chats, group chats, or external chats and meetings.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The Purview page lists data loss prevention as unsupported for Facilitator AI interactions.
claims.quote: | Data loss prevention | ✕ |

claims.claim: The Purview page lists sensitivity labels as unsupported for Facilitator AI interactions.
claims.quote: | Sensitivity labels | ✕ |

claims.claim: Purview DLP can block Copilot external web search for prompts containing configured sensitive information.
claims.quote: When a user prompt contains the configured SITs, Copilot and Cowork block external web search as a grounding source and continue to generate the response using allowed internal Microsoft 365 data sources.

claims.claim: The Copilot DLP web-search control is not confirmed to cover Facilitator.
claims.quote: Searched: "Facilitator" "web search" "DLP". Opened purview/ai-teams-facilitator (DLP unsupported) and purview/dlp-microsoft365-copilot-location-learn-about (Copilot, Copilot Chat and Cowork; no Facilitator inclusion).

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented what Facilitator's proactive capability sends to the search service.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Facilitator proactive web search Bing generated queries privacy meeting conversation. Opened microsoftteams/facilitator-teams and copilot/plan/manage-public-web-access; neither specifies the proactive Facilitator query payload.

claims.claim: Learn's Copilot web-search page describes generated queries sent to the Bing search service.
claims.quote: Based on these terms, Copilot generates a search query that it sends to the Bing search service asking for more information.

claims.claim: The Copilot web-search page excludes generated web search queries from the Data Protection Addendum.
claims.quote: The Microsoft Products and Services Data Protection Addendum (DPA) doesn't apply to the use of generated web search queries in Microsoft Copilot, Microsoft Copilot Chat, or the Bing search service.

claims.claim: Whether the cited Copilot web-search privacy terms cover Facilitator's proactive searches remains unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams Facilitator proactive web search Bing generated queries privacy meeting conversation. Read microsoftteams/facilitator-teams and copilot/plan/manage-public-web-access; the latter names Copilot, Copilot Chat, Researcher, Analyst and Cowork, not Facilitator.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost; Open questions
claims.claim: No separate price, meter or credit rate is published for proactive Facilitator question answering.
claims.quote: Searched: Facilitator detects answers questions pricing meter Copilot credits capacity licensing; "Facilitator" pricing licensing capacity Microsoft 365 Copilot. Opened facilitator-teams, copilot-license-options and Copilot Studio requirements-messages-management; no proactive Facilitator meter.

claims.claim: The notice describes no action for this capability beyond searching and posting an answer.
claims.quote: Searched: "Facilitator" "proactive" "web" "policy". Read the full MC1409304 notice and microsoftteams/facilitator-teams; the notice describes detecting needs, searching and posting responses, not another action of this capability.

claims.claim: If Allow web search in Copilot is not configured, web search is available to users in the commercial scope described.
claims.quote: If the IT admin doesn't configure the Allow web search in Copilot policy, web search will be available to users in both Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft Copilot Chat

claims.claim: That unconfigured-policy availability has an exception when optional connected experiences are Disabled.
claims.quote: unless the IT admin has set the Allow the use of additional optional connected experiences in Office policy to Disabled.

claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Apps admin center path reaches Configure Settings for Cloud Policy.
claims.quote: Under Customization, select Policy Management. On the Policy configurations page, select Create. ... On the Configure Settings page, select the policies that you want to include in the policy configuration.
claims.fix: Extend controls[0].ui.path and its rendered counterpart to 'Customization > Policy Management > Policy configurations > Create > Start with the basics > Choose the scope > Configure Settings > Allow web search in Copilot'. The Cloud Policy page says to search policies by name, and the already cited https://learn.microsoft.com/copilot/plan/manage-public-web-access names this policy.

claims.claim: Allow web search in Copilot is the documented Cloud Policy control for Copilot web search.
claims.quote: The primary way that IT admins can control access to web search is by using the Allow web search in Copilot policy, which is available only in Cloud Policy service for Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: POST /beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors can apply a desired-state baseline once.
claims.quote: Create a new configurationMonitor object ... applies a desired-state baseline once in applyOnce mode. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/admin/configurationManagement/configurationMonitors

claims.claim: This API is a preview beta API not supported for production use.
claims.quote: APIs under the /beta version in Microsoft Graph are subject to change. Use of these APIs in production applications is not supported.

claims.claim: Setting mode to applyOnce applies the baseline on behalf of the signed-in administrator.
claims.quote: An active applyOnce monitor runs in the background on behalf of the signed-in administrator and then becomes inactive.

claims.claim: The web-search baseline resource type is microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch.
claims.quote: "resourceType": "microsoft.copilot.allowwebsearch"

claims.claim: The baseline resourceVersion is 1.
claims.quote: "resourceVersion": 1

claims.claim: The resource's properties.value is a string accepting 0, 1 or 2.
claims.quote: The value property is a string, not a Boolean or a number. ... | value | Write | String | ... | 0, 1, 2 |

claims.claim: Value 0 enables web search in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: 0 enables it in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: Value 1 disables web search in both Copilot and Copilot Chat.
claims.quote: 1 disables it in both.

claims.claim: Value 2 disables web search in Copilot Work mode while leaving Web mode and Copilot Chat enabled.
claims.quote: 2 disables it in Microsoft 365 Copilot Work mode while enabling it in Microsoft 365 Copilot Web mode and Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat.

claims.claim: The TCM preview supports these Copilot resources only in tenant-level Cloud Policy policies.
claims.quote: TCM supports these settings only in tenant-level policies in the Microsoft 365 Apps admin center.

claims.claim: TCM operations fail for the resource if the setting is configured in a group-level policy.
claims.quote: Before using TCM, ensure that the target setting isn't configured in any group-level policy in that admin center. If it is, monitoring, snapshots, remediation, and applyOnce fail for that resource.

claims.claim: The TCM service principal needs delegated CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite for remediation and applyOnce.
claims.quote: Grant the following Microsoft Graph permissions to the TCM service principal. ... Delegated permissions ... | Remediation and applyOnce | CopilotPolicySettings.ReadWrite |

claims.claim: The calling app needs delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All for applyOnce.
claims.quote: Creating an applyOnce monitor supports delegated permissions only. In addition to the calling app's delegated ConfigurationMonitoring.ReadWrite.All permission

claims.claim: AI Administrator is the required least-privileged signed-in user role for applying the web-search resource.
claims.quote: For remediation and applyOnce, AI Administrator is the least-privileged Microsoft Entra role for the signed-in user. This role requirement applies to the user, not to the TCM service principal.

claims.claim: The notice names the Copilot web search setting but does not identify the Allow web search in Copilot policy or its mode-specific option.
claims.quote: The feature depends on the Copilot web search setting. If web search is disabled, responses are not generated.

claims.claim: No separate tenant UI or API switch for proactive question detection and answers is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Facilitator proactive question detection knowledge gaps separate admin setting Teams PowerShell policy web search; "Facilitator" "proactive" "PowerShell" "Graph" setting. Read facilitator-teams, app-centric-management, Update-M365TeamsApp and Copilot TCM resources; no separate switch.

claims.claim: Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention Policies is the documented Purview route for Facilitator retention policies.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft Purview portal, navigate to Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention Policies and create a retention policy
claims.fix: Extend controls[2].ui.path and its rendered counterpart to 'Solutions > Data Lifecycle Management > Policies > Retention policies > New retention policy > Assign admin units > Choose the type of retention policy to create > Static > Choose locations to apply the policy > Teams chats > Decide if you want to retain content, delete it, or both'. This is the static-policy route documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/create-retention-policies; add that URL to sources. Keep the existing Facilitator docs link, which supports the original route and applicability.

claims.claim: New-RetentionComplianceRule can add a Keep rule with a duration in days to an existing named retention policy.
claims.quote: The retention rule must be added to an existing retention policy using the Policy parameter. ... RetentionComplianceAction ... Keep ... RetentionDuration ... An integer: The hold duration in days.

claims.claim: The retention-rule name must be specified as required by the reference.
claims.quote: The Name parameter specifies a unique name for the retention rule. ... Parameter sets Default ... Mandatory: True

claims.claim: A retention policy with Teams chats governs Facilitator AI interactions in meetings.
claims.quote: For Facilitator AI interactions in meetings, use a retention policy with the Teams chats option.

claims.claim: New-RetentionCompliancePolicy creates a retention policy that also requires New-RetentionComplianceRule.
claims.quote: Use the New-RetentionCompliancePolicy cmdlet to create new retention policies and new retention label policies in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal. Creating a new policy also requires use of the New-RetentionComplianceRule cmdlet.

claims.claim: For migrated tenants the app-centric route reaches Facilitator's Edit availability control.
claims.quote: Select the Users and groups tab. Under Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization, select Availability. Select Edit availability. Select the required option from Available to menu.
claims.fix: Replace the prose route with 'Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Facilitator > Users and groups > Select to manage who this app is installed for or available to in your organization > Availability > Edit availability > Available to', using the already cited https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoftteams/app-centric-management. The printed steps are correct, but omit the section heading and stop before the availability choice.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp is documented for managing app availability in app-centric management.
claims.quote: You can't update app availability in bulk in Teams admin center, but you can do so through PowerShell. For more information on PowerShell cmdlets for app availability, see Update-M365TeamsApp.

claims.claim: The Teams admin center documents Allow or Block for Facilitator as a whole.
claims.quote: In the left rail navigation, select Teams apps > Manage apps. ... Select Facilitator from the app list. In the actions menu, select Allow or Block.

claims.claim: Learn calls for Teams admin credentials to allow or block Facilitator.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Teams admin center with your Teams admin credentials.

claims.claim: Blocking the Facilitator app blocks its broader features, not just proactive answers.
claims.quote: As an admin, you control whether Facilitator is available to your entire organization or to a certain group of users. ... To allow or block Facilitator for users, complete the following steps

claims.claim: Facilitator is blocked when all apps are blocked for the organization.
claims.quote: Facilitator is allowed by default. However, if all apps are blocked for your organization, Facilitator is also blocked.

claims.claim: Learn describes app permission policies for allowing Facilitator to a group of users.
claims.quote: To allow Facilitator for users, a new app policy needs to be created and then assigned to users. Follow the instructions at Use app permission policies to control user access to apps to create a new app policy for Facilitator.

claims.claim: Learn describes app-centric management for assigning Facilitator availability to users.
claims.quote: Follow the instructions at Add or modify app availability for users to assign the policy to users using app-centric management.

claims.claim: The Set-CsTeamsAppPermissionPolicy warning requires creation and modification of app permission policies in the Teams admin center.
claims.quote: We require that all creation and modification of app permission polices (not including the assignment or removal of policies from users) happens in the Microsoft Teams & Skype for Business Admin Center

claims.claim: App-centric management replaces the older permission-policy mechanism.
claims.quote: App permissions are a different concept from permission policies, which app centric management is replacing.

claims.claim: Purview auditing supports Facilitator, including questions and answers for meetings.
claims.quote: Auditing and AI interactions ... AI app-specific information: Facilitator AI-generated notes, moderation, and questions and answers for meetings are supported.

claims.claim: Purview eDiscovery supports Facilitator, including questions and answers for meetings.
claims.quote: eDiscovery and AI interactions ... Facilitator AI-generated notes, moderation, and questions and answers for meetings are supported with a KeyQL query.

claims.claim: Purview Data Lifecycle Management supports Facilitator AI interactions.
claims.quote: | Data Lifecycle Management | ✓ | ... For Facilitator AI interactions in meetings, use a retention policy with the Teams chats option.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp modifies app availability.
claims.quote: This cmdlet allows administrators to modify app state, availability and installation status by adding or removing users and groups or changing assignment type or installation status.
